source_hierarchy: Current assigned 32-page CORE; applicable original-core Living FAQ corrections supersede conflicting original wording. FAQ pages are broad; excluded modules do not enter scope.
novelty_policy: New source-supported rule, defined outcome branch, or timing/exception interaction; no cosmetic/numerical variants. Preserve all earlier frozen entries.

stopping_rule.claim: Working source-clause saturation under original standard-core scope and strict novelty, subject to fresh complete source/key/asked-map challenge. Prior rejected claims preserved.

book_passages.passage: Fear through Fear / each player / land order
Gameplay tips and optional reminder techniques
Track icons and full turn order reference

faq_rulings.rule: Add exactly one additional Blight to the initial pool, regardless of player count. With a Healthy Island card use 2 per player +1; without a card use 5 per player +1. This extra one is added only during setup, never again when a Blight card flips.
All Blight placed on the island during setup comes from the box, not from the pool on the card/Invader Board. The initial pool starts full unless an instruction explicitly says otherwise.
The initial Explore is the last part of ordinary setup; the first Spirit Phase follows it. It resolves an Explore Card, but is not the Explore Step of an Invader Phase.
If multiple choices equally satisfy a Spirit's setup instructions, the player chooses among them.

Separate Presence setup instructions may place Presence in the same land; there is no default requirement to select different lands. Three or more Presence in one land still make only one Sacred Site.
Every original Spirit can be used in solo play, including Ocean and Bringer.
Use 13 Presence disks of each color. Any accidental extra disk in a printing is a spare.

Each individual Spirit must complete Growth, then gain Energy, then play/pay for Power Cards. Different Spirits need not do these steps in lockstep and may wait for one another's Growth results. All must finish the Spirit Phase before Fast Powers begin.

Do everything in a chosen Growth option, if possible, in any order. If part is impossible, do as much as possible; inability to complete a benefit does not prohibit choosing the option. An explicit cost, if any, must be paid in full.
Multiple Presence placements in one Growth may be chained: the Presence just placed can serve as the origin for the next placement.

Whenever adding Presence from a track, the Spirit may instead reposition its Presence already on the island, even before the tracks are empty. Choose a legal destination measured from the current board position, then take the disk from any island land, including the origin disk.

A Move Presence Growth icon moves one disk up to the indicated distance from its current land. Repositioning instead of adding from a track can take the disk from anywhere. Ocean Gather/Push uses ordinary adjacent-land movement and is mandatory.
Rampant Green may gain a Power Card before deciding where to place the Presence from its always-performed Jungle/Wetland Growth instruction.
Energy gained during the Fast Power Phase cannot pay for the ordinary Power Cards that had to be played and paid for in the completed Spirit Phase.
Unused Energy carries over between turns; only the things specified in Time Passes are cleared.
There is no maximum hand size and players may show their Power Cards to one another.
Power Progressions and matching colored card corners are learning aids for beginners; low-complexity Spirits do not have to use them in ordinary play.
An effect allowing a Power Card to be played mid-turn does not itself resolve that Power unless explicitly stated. The card is resolved at its speed in the appropriate phase, outside another action.
Cards played by an effect outside the Spirit Phase's ordinary play-and-pay action are additional to the Presence-track card-play limit.

Whenever gaining a Major Power, Forget one Power Card unless specifically exempted. It can be from hand, discard, in play, or the newly gained Major itself. A transfer/gift is not a Gain, and taking a card follows its explicit exemption.
One card cannot be Forgotten to pay two separate Forgetting requirements. Each gained Major requires its own Forget.
A Forgotten Unique Power is not normally available again; recovery requires an explicit instruction.
Choose each Power's target when using/resolving that Power, not when playing its card. A changed board state may require a different legal target.
A Power may target a land where its instructions will do nothing, provided the Range and Target restrictions are satisfied.
Foregoing all text effects means not using or targeting the Power. To use/target it, attempt its effects; they need not actually change anything.

An innate whose only available thresholds change its own Speed/Range cannot be used/targeted. It must have an instruction with potential to affect the game state, even if that instruction does nothing in the particular chosen land.
Elements uncovered on a Presence track or obtained by playing a card are usable immediately, including mid-turn. Losing the track benefit or the card immediately loses those Elements.
An Any Element on a Presence track may be chosen later in the turn, but once chosen cannot change that turn. Flexible Elements directly gained by an action are chosen when gained.

Resolve thresholds in printed order. Elements gained/lost while resolving can affect later thresholds; already resolved or missed thresholds are not revisited. Speed/Range/target modifiers are checked when needed before their affected checks.

An innate is one Power with one target, not separate Powers per threshold. Resolve every threshold met in order unless an Instead effect replaces earlier effects. You may pretend to have fewer Elements for the entire Power, not separately for individual thresholds.
Extra copies of threshold Elements do not allow extra uses of an innate. Powers are normally once per turn; additional uses require an explicit Repeat instruction.

Elements are not spent on a threshold, so a Repeat normally meets it again if the Elements remain. Repeating does not double the printed Elements of a card; an explicit gain-Elements effect can occur again.
Repeating counts as using a new Power, while not counting as playing another Power Card. The erroneous not in fourth/fifth-printing rules must be removed.

Ordinary Repeats obey normal origin/Range/Target restrictions and may choose a different legal target. A Repeat specifying where to use it instead obeys that location instruction, overriding ordinary Range/Target restrictions.

Powerstorm/Gift of Strength grant a Spirit an option usable later this turn. Choose the Power Card when repeating it, not when the option is granted. A Slow card can be repeated during the Slow Phase. The chosen card may enter play after the once-this-turn permission was granted; it is a Spirit permission rather than a grant-time card snapshot.
A Repeat uses the Power's most recently assigned Speed, normally the speed of its original use. A Repeat explicitly instructed to occur immediately follows that timing.
Range/Speed changes persist for Repeats. Do not apply an internal Range boost twice. Shadows need not pay its Range-ignoring Energy cost again for an ordinary Repeat of the modified Power.
Ignore Repeat instructions when repeating a Power. Repeating Powerstorm can still grant its Energy, but cannot grant another round of Repeats.
Powerstorm and Gift of Strength explicitly Repeat a Power Card and cannot Repeat an innate.
Powerstorm's threshold allows up to three different Power Cards to be repeated; it does not permit the same card to be repeated three times by that use.
A slash between piece types means either or both types within the stated total. Push up to 3 Explorer/Town moves at most three pieces combined, not three of each.
Invader means an Explorer, Town, or City. Counting Invaders counts each piece equally; remove 2 Invaders may remove two Cities unless the instruction restricts the choice.
Health and Damage are separate totals: taking Damage does not lower Health. If a Health reduction makes Damage already on a piece reach its new Health, destroy it immediately.
Allocate Damage to Invaders as desired; there is no requirement to hit Explorers first or finish a particular building first. Partial Damage heals in Time Passes.
Partly damaged Invaders and Dahan still deal full normal Damage: 1/2/3 for Explorer/Town/City and 2 per Dahan, absent explicit modifiers.
Explicit Fear from a Power and normal Fear for actual Town/City destruction both apply. Shatter Homesteads can generate its printed 1 Fear plus 1 for the destroyed Town.
Earned Fear Cards are ordinarily revealed when resolved during the Invader Phase. Flip the earned stack and resolve one at a time in earned order, without looking ahead.
Resolve only the effect for the current Terror Level, even if the card was earned at a lower level. Do not also resolve lower-level effects.
A Fear Card earned during Fear resolution goes at the bottom of the resolving stack and resolves in that Invader Phase. If earning it raises Terror Level, subsequent Fear Cards use that new level.

Each player choices on Fear Cards may affect any land allowed by the card. No default own-Presence restriction exists. If a card requires Presence/a Sacred Site, any Spirit's qualifies unless it explicitly refers to a particular Spirit's.
Successive players may move the same piece again when a Fear Card allows it, subject to all explicit restrictions, including any requirement to choose different lands.

Dahan Enheartened levels II/III choose different lands, Gather up to 2 Dahan, then deal respectively 1 Damage if Dahan are present / 1 Damage per Dahan present. Gathering zero is allowed in a land that already has Dahan.
Damage listed by Dahan Raid and Dahan Enheartened is total Damage in the affected land, not that much to each Invader.
Trade Suffers at Terror Level III only replaces a Town or City in a Coastal land. The Coastal modifier applies to both options.

Overseas Trade Seems Safer level II skips a Coastal Build that would normally add a City: add neither City nor Town. If a Town would normally be built, build it. The skip determination precedes Build modifications.
Scapegoats levels II/III resolve one action per land with Towns/Cities. At II destroy 1 Explorer per Town and 2 per City. At III destroy all Explorers, then 1 Town per City.

Island-wide/all-lands-class effects such as Dahan on their Guard check the current contents when the ongoing effect matters. Encompassing Ward follows the target Spirit's current Presence. Single-land (or land-and-neighbors) effects generally fix their value when used.
No standard per-land stacking limit applies to any piece. Many Presence of one Spirit still count as one Sacred Site in that land.
Destroyed Presence is not returned to the Spirit Panel and cannot normally be added during Growth. Only an effect explicitly allowing destroyed Presence can restore it.
Presence may be added/moved into a land that already contains Blight. Blight destroys Presence when it is added, not continuously.
Each addition of one or more Blight destroys one Presence of every Spirit there, not one per token; separate additions destroy Presence again. Cascades remain within the original action tree.

An ordinary Ravage causing 2 or more Damage to the land adds exactly one Blight, regardless of how high the Damage is. A cascade adds one extra Blight to one adjacent land and continues only if that land already had Blight.

When the Healthy Island side empties, add the newly revealed side's specified Blight per player as a fresh supply. Do not treat that number as the total pool for both sides. Do not apply the setup +1 again.

If an action must add more Blight simultaneously than remains on the Healthy side, flip immediately, carry any remaining old Blight into the new pool, fully resolve immediate flip effects, then add the required Blight.
Explore adds one Explorer to every accessible matching land even if it already has Invaders. A Town/City in that land is a source. Multiple sources never add multiple Explorers.
The Coastal Lands Invader Card affects all Coastal lands for its Explore, later Build, and later Ravage, subject to each action's normal restrictions.
A two-terrain Invader Card affects all eligible lands of both terrain types, not a choice between the types.
Players choose the order of affected lands for each Invader Card, including interleaving the two shown terrains of a Stage III card.

Determine which lands an Invader Card affects before resolving its individual land actions. Changes during earlier land actions do not add new affected lands for that same card. New Invaders in an already queued Ravage do participate when it resolves.
If the entire Ravage is skipped/prevented, Dahan do not counterattack. Defend reducing Damage to zero does not skip the Ravage: surviving Dahan still counterattack.

Invaders damage land and Dahan separately, equally, and simultaneously, then surviving Dahan fight back. Losing Earth's Sacred Site to that Blight does not retroactively remove the Defend protecting Dahan from that same Ravage.
Defend reduces both Damage to the land and Damage to the Dahan by the full Defend amount; it is not divided between the two recipients.
Ignore the Stage II flag/Escalation symbol when not playing with an Adversary.
A Year of Perfect Stillness/Paralyzing Fright skipping actions in a land does not prevent that land's Towns/Cities from being exploration sources for adjacent lands.
Earning the last Fear Card reveals Victory; resolving that last card's text is unnecessary to win.
Check victory and defeat after the current action and all actions it triggers are complete. Do not finish all Ravages on the card. Meeting both win and loss conditions then is a sacrifice victory.

Swiftness of Lightning can make one Power Fast per Air Element currently available; innate Thundering Destruction is also a Power eligible for conversion. Re-check current Air and prior uses if Elements change.
Swiftness of Lightning is used during the Fast Power Phase.
Harbingers of the Lightning generates its conditional Fear in the target land, not in a land the Dahan are pushed to.
River's Domain can make River's single Wetland Presence a Sacred Site, but it is still only one Presence disk.
When an effect moves/affects a Sacred Site, River may choose one or two Presence for a Wetland Sacred Site.
In true solo, a Power targeting Another Spirit may target yourself, but conditional extra benefits requiring a different Spirit do not apply.

Pay Shadows of the Dahan's 1 Energy when resolving a Power to ignore the numeric Range to a target land with Dahan. Source restrictions such as Sacred Site and all other Target requirements remain. It does not modify Range arrows inside the effect text.
Mantle of Dread's target Spirit chooses one of its lands even if it has only an Explorer or only a Town. It is not forced to select a different land containing both.
Crops Wither and Fade always generates 2 Fear; the or divides only the adjacent replacement clauses, so choose whether to replace a City or a Town.
Using Choke the Land with Green is optional. Its omitted may in fourth/fifth printings does not force Presence destruction whenever it could skip a Build/Ravage.
Steady Regeneration's Healthy/Blighted condition refers to the island/Blight Card state, not whether the destination land contains Blight.
Fields Choked with Growth's fixed-number Gather/Push instructions move the stated number if possible, or as many as possible. Only up to permits an arbitrary smaller number.
Ally of the Dahan can move one of Thunderspeaker's Presence with each Dahan moved by Gather, Push or other Move effects. Moving two Dahan can carry two Presence.

Sworn to Victory triggers for each Dahan destroyed by a Ravage even if no Blight was added. Finish the entire land's Ravage, including Blight, cascades, Presence loss and counterattack, then destroy Thunderspeaker Presence within Range 1 as instructed.
When a Power moves Dahan into an Ocean currently in play, Thunderspeaker may move its Presence along with them.

Ocean in Play Drowns humans after they are moved into an Ocean on a board where Ocean has any Presence. Ocean need not have Presence in that Ocean. Drowned Invaders are destroyed immediately, generate normal building Fear immediately, and are then stored for Energy conversion.

Exchange drowned Invaders' unmodified Health for Energy at X Health per Energy, where X is the player count. Change is allowed, e.g., in 2-player play a City can yield 1 Energy with 1 Explorer retained. Drowned Dahan give no Energy.
An active Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for Powers and Blight, not generally for Fear Cards or ordinary Invader actions. A Fear Card cannot normally add/move an Invader there just because it is in play.
An Ocean in play may receive Blight, including as a cascade destination.

Ocean's third Growth cannot add Presence to the Ocean by treating it as a Coastal Wetland: Growth is not a Power. Existing Presence in an Ocean may nevertheless be used as a Range origin during Growth.

In the original base set, Indomitable Claim can put Ocean Presence inland because it explicitly ignores land-type restrictions. Generic Presence-adding Powers do not bypass Ocean's placement restriction.
Powers and Special Rules may measure Range through an Ocean in play as a land.

If Ocean loses its last Presence on a board during an action, that Ocean remains a land until the action and all its triggered actions finish. Thereafter non-human pieces remain physically there but out of play until the Ocean returns to play; humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land.

If Ocean in Play triggers but fails to destroy a moved human, Push it to a non-Ocean land as part of that triggered action; Ocean gains no Energy. If a human remains illegally in the Ocean after the action tree, clean it up to the nearest legal land.

Tidal Boon's conditional if Dahan are pushed applies only to the Push in that use of the Power, not later Pushes all turn. The target Spirit may choose one of its lands without a Town and still Push Dahan.

To Dream a Thousand Deaths modifies explicit Damage/Destroy effects of Bringer's Powers. They cause the prescribed nightmare Fear/Push rather than actual Damage/destruction, regardless of whether the Power says Dahan or another Spirit deals that Damage.

Resolve each Bringer Power in its own imagined normal-resolution state. Damage instructions within one Power may combine to determine what it would destroy; Damage from separate Powers or Repeats does not accumulate. A Repeat can earn Fear again for the same Invader.

Bringer can exploit real prior Damage: 1 nightmare Damage to a City already bearing 2 real Damage earns its City Fear. It neither heals nor adds actual Damage, so multiple separate qualifying Powers may each earn Fear for that same damaged City.

Bringer's player may deal real Damage with Fear Cards, and Dahan counterattack normally after Bringer provides Defend. Bringer may add real Blight that destroys Presence. Explicit Damage/Destroy instructions against Dahan in Bringer's own Powers do nothing to the Dahan.

A nightmare destruction is not an actual destruction for later checks: Mists of Oblivion earns no bonus Fear for an allegedly destroyed building, and Vengeance of the Dead does not trigger merely from that nightmare.
Bringer may Push a virtually destroyed Town into an Ocean in play; Ocean then actually Drowns it. This gives 2 nightmare Fear plus 1 actual destruction Fear.

Bringer may indirectly cause real destruction by lowering Health, moving an already-damaged piece out of a Health bonus, or replacing it with a lower-Health piece; these are not its explicit Damage/Destroy instructions. Triggers check after the Power completes.
Spirits May Yet Dream may reveal any Fear Card: already earned, on top of the deck, or deeper in it.

Call on Midnight's Dreams refers to itself when it says this Power. Forgetting it as the ordinary Major-gain Forget also satisfies its conditional; a second Forget is unnecessary. Once Forgotten it cannot later be repeated by a once-this-turn option.

Vengeance of the Dead's base effect is 3 Fear, then after each completed effect/action destroying Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. It triggers after the whole Power/action resolves, not between its printed Damage instructions.

A Vengeance of the Dead trigger cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Two separate uses create separate triggers that can trigger one another, but each branch stops before re-triggering the same trigger.
Tsunami's threshold generates its extra Fear separately for each other Coastal land affected, normally two extra Fear on an ordinary board.
Poisoned Land resolves in printed order, so its threshold counts the Blight added by its own earlier instruction.
Veil the Night's Hunt must assign its per-Dahan Damage to different Invaders. If there are fewer Invaders than Dahan, each receives 1 Damage and the rest is wasted.
Song of Sanctity is Slow. Missing artwork around its Energy cost in second/third printings does not change its turtle Speed symbol.
Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship's third line says Push all Explorers from target land; fourth/fifth printings omitted the Explorer symbol.
Damage dealt by Invaders to each other under Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship is simultaneous; they can destroy one another.

Infinite Vitality's threshold protects Dahan in its land from Damage and Destroy effects, but not Remove/Replace. The land may still be chosen as a Blight destination; the Power changes what happens when Blight would be added, not which land may be chosen.
Wrap in Wings of Sunlight can Move Dahan to their own land, which counts as a Move. Moving zero Dahan does not grant Defend because no destination land was selected by an actual move.

For The Trees and Stones Speak of War's threshold, each Dahan actually Pushed carries Defend 2 from the target land. That is fixed Defend 2 per moved Dahan, not Defend 2 per Dahan already in its destination; later movement by another Power does not carry it again.

Entwined Power shares Presence only for meeting Range/Target restrictions. Combined Presence can qualify as a Sacred Site for targeting, but does not create Sacred Sites for other effects or share ownership of Presence. River's Domain remains River's own special rule.
In true solo, Entwined Power can target yourself and gain two Power Cards; with its threshold it grants 6 Energy.

A Spirit using a transferred card follows as much of its text as legally possible. If it says Drown, Ocean's defined Drown effect still works: the acting Spirit destroys the Invader and then places it on Ocean's mat.

Range boosts do not extend effects requiring one of your lands/a land with your Presence, because that is a contents restriction rather than a numeric Range. A Power's ordinary numeric target Range can be boosted without changing additional own-Presence clauses.
A land is not adjacent to itself; it is at Range 0 of itself and within any positive Range. It can be its own nearest land meeting a condition.

After an action and pending triggers finish, human pieces in an illegal place are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. This is neither Move, Remove nor Destroy and triggers nothing. Non-human pieces in an existing illegal location remain but are out of play until legal again.
A damaged piece that dies because it moved out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty is destroyed in the destination land, not in an in-between state.
A outnumbers B can be true when there are no B, provided there is at least one A. Thus Dahan can outnumber Towns/Cities in a land with none.
Invader components are unlimited. If figures run out, represent additional pieces using Energy markers or other clear substitutes.

A single action removing N Health worth of Invaders scaling with a condition uses one combined Health limit, rather than batches. Separate each-player removals remain separate actions and may not pool their limits.
A threshold saying +N Damage adds that much overall Damage when the threshold resolves. It is not extra Damage to each Invader unless the text explicitly says so.

Mists of Oblivion's 1 Damage to each Town/City normally destroys them only if they were already damaged or additional threshold Damage is applied. Its bonus Fear depends on actual destructions caused by that use.
Fear from a Spirit-targeting Power is not generated in any specific land unless the Power says so. Mantle of Dread's Fear therefore does not add Defend via Dread Apparitions.
A Damage boost increases the original source's Damage; destruction from boosted Damage still counts as being caused by that Power for its own conditional effects.

Nothing happens to the Dahan from those explicit Damage/Destroy instructions. Ignore those instructions and resolve the rest of the Power normally. Bringer’s Invader nightmare Fear/Push outcomes do not apply to Dahan. This answer concerns explicit Damage/Destroy instructions; it does not prohibit the indirect Health-rule destruction already tested by Q86.

General Power Range boosts can affect printed numeric Range arrows in targeting and effect text, obeying restrictions; they do not boost a Range boost or another Spirit's actions. Shadows changes targeting Range only. Excluded Sky example removed in v6. Linked precise primary source qualifies old broad wording explicitly in v8/Q105 key-corrections.json.

The existing Range change persists for the Repeat, but the internal threshold does not add another +1 Range. The Repeat keeps the prior boost even if the Elements needed for that threshold have since been lost. This is the specific published interpretation of internal Range boosts, rather than stacking the modifier each use.

A Repeat does not count as playing another Power Card, so it does not increase a count of cards played such as Boon of Vigor and does not spend another ordinary Card Play. It does count as using a new Power. Any payment required by the Repeat permission is separate from playing another card.

No. Effects moving, destroying or otherwise doing things with Presence affect Presence on the island unless they explicitly say otherwise. Choose island Presence for that instruction; it does not remove a track disk or reveal a track benefit.

source_refs.label: CORE p.13 Presence and Sacred Sites

faq_rulings.rule: Take a random Blight Card, place it Healthy Island side up, and do not look at its back during setup. It is not a free choice of a preferred known reverse effect.

source_refs.label: CORE p.6 Invader Board setup step 5

faq_rulings.rule: Yes, unless explicitly specified otherwise by that innate. Innates are automatically available every turn and do not normally cost Energy or consume Card Plays; they are not cards that must be played from hand. Meet the Elements and other normal timing/target requirements. The usual once-per-turn restriction still applies.

No to both. A Power ordinarily has one use that turn; paying its printed cost again grants no extra use. Making a Slow Power Fast gives its normal use in Fast, not an additional use in each phase. An explicit Repeat or other stated exception is needed for another use.

source_refs.label: CORE p.17 One Land! One Turn! One Use!, last bullet

faq_rulings.rule: Add a direct FAQ ruling/source mapping; existing question and key already test the rule. No new question.
Add a direct FAQ ruling/source mapping; existing question and key already test the rule. No new question.
Add a direct FAQ ruling/source mapping for Blazing Renewal destination dependency; existing question and key already test it. No new question.

Ocean In Play Pushes the surviving Dahan to a non-Ocean land as part of its own triggered action. This is an actual Push, capable of triggering applicable movement effects; it is not the later non-action cleanup operation. Cleanup only handles a piece still illegally placed after the action tree. No expansion effect or piece is needed for this branch: the FAQ expressly supplies Infinite Vitality threshold on the Ocean as a core-game case.

It need not keep its original target. The Spirit may choose any valid target by the ordinary Range and Target rules, either the original land or a different legal land. Only a Repeat that specifies its destination replaces those normal restrictions with the specified-location instruction.
Concealing Shadows prevents Dahan Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn; does not reduce land Damage or prevent counterattack. Direct Destroy and other-source Damage are outside its protection.

The simultaneous addition destroys one Presence from each Spirit, even though two Blight tokens are added. Two separate additions destroy one Presence per Spirit on each addition, hence two per Spirit if available. Cascades elsewhere are outside the requested count.

source_refs.label: .7w4g8nw; especially Each time you add one or more Blight

faq_rulings.rule: Concealing Shadows does not prevent them: its protection is only against Damage from Ravaging Invaders, while Poisoned Land explicitly Destroys Dahan. Infinite Vitality's threshold makes those Dahan ignore Damage and Destruction effects, so it prevents that destruction.

Direct Spirit Power Damage is not reduced by Defend, so those Dahan take 2 Damage in the Defend-only case. Concealing Shadows also does not prevent it because it only protects from Ravaging Invaders. Infinite Vitality’s threshold does prevent that Damage. In the separate Invader Ravage case, Defend 3 reduces 2 to zero for both land and Dahan, not negative Damage.

source_refs.label: CORE p.18 Defend; especially reduces Damage done by Invaders and Whenever Invaders deal Damage
CORE p.18 explicit Damage recipient rule

faq_rulings.rule: The grant stays +2; Range boosts do not increase another Range boost. Reaching Grasp’s Power-only bonus applies to B’s Powers, including Innates and Power Cards, subject to the normal Range-arrow restrictions. It does not extend ordinary Growth, which is not a Power; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth.
source_refs: Primary original Reaching Grasp face: card-scope-source/reaching_grasp.jpg

faq_rulings.rule: For a land-targeting Power, measure the internal arrow from the target land unless otherwise specified. For a Spirit-targeting Power, normally measure from the Presence of the Spirit following the instruction, B here, unless the text says otherwise. Apply the bonuses of the Power user A, not B: the stated Range 1 becomes Range 3 from B’s Presence. Blazing Renewal explicitly measures from the Power user A’s Presence, even when B adds Presence; its explicit origin overrides the default.

Its printed Elements remain while the card is in play and can support Innates even though its text was not used. The paid Energy is not refunded. Foregoing the text does not remove/discard the card immediately; it stays in play and is normally discarded during Time Passes, when its Elements go away.

source_refs.label: CORE p17 General Principle: You Can Skip Using A Power's Effect
CORE p16 Anatomy of Powers, Elements Gained: Elements last while card is in play
CORE p10 Time Passes: discard played cards and clear Elements

faq_rulings.rule: Defend is not expended: it reduces each Ravage by 3 for the entire turn. Each deals 1 Damage to land and 1 to Dahan. Land Damage below 2 is ignored per occurrence, so the two 1-Damage land results never combine into Blight. The Dahan’s first 1 Damage persists until Time Passes; the second 1 reaches its 2 Health and destroys it before a second counterattack.

source_refs.label: CORE p18 Defend: Whenever Invaders deal Damage; Defend effects last for the entire turn
CORE p9 Ravage: Damage reduction, simultaneous recipients, and Partial Damage to the land is ignored

faq_rulings.rule: Yes to both. The Spirit may resolve the first Power as if it had fewer Elements, consistently for that entire Power, and must resolve the base effect plus all thresholds met by that assumed set. The hypothetical reduction does not spend or remove actual Elements, so another Power may still use the actual 3 Water. It is not permission to select or skip individual threshold instructions independently.

source_refs.label: CORE p17 Elemental Thresholds: may always resolve a Power as if fewer Elements; Elements not used up
FAQ Core .bu6od0c footnote 1: explicitly may activate only lower innate level; entire-Power consistency

faq_rulings.rule: It must choose one entire Growth option and perform all possible actions in that option. It may not combine actions from separate options or select multiple options without an explicit instruction permitting that. The actions within the chosen option may be performed in any order.

source_refs.label: CORE p.8 Spirit Phase, Grow step: Choose one option; Each section is a single choice

faq_rulings.rule: Both A and B are legal targets. Printed Range 1 is a maximum, so Range 0 is allowed: A contains your Presence and B is one land away. The Power does not have to target a land exactly one away.

source_refs.label: CORE p.16 Anatomy of Powers, Range: This is a maximum; you can always use a shorter Range

faq_rulings.rule: Yes. Powerstorm grants the Spirit a general once-this-turn Repeat option, not a permission restricted to cards already in play at grant time. The new Major is eligible once it is in play; Bringer can pay its cost and Repeat it at its current Speed. Forgetting Call on Midnight’s Dream does not remove the separate new Major.

No. There is no default stacking limit for any piece, so crowding alone cannot prevent those otherwise legal additions or movements. Each specific action must still obey its normal instructions. A large Presence stack still forms only one Sacred Site for that Spirit in that land.

The option must be chosen before either option begins resolving. Bringer cannot inspect the Major Power draw and then switch to the 2 Fear option. If the Major-gain option is chosen, resolve that option, including the ordinary draw-four/keep-one and Major Forgetting requirement; drawing the cards is already resolving that option.

The Spirit must complete Growth, then gain normal Energy, then play and pay for Power Cards. It may not take the normal income or actually play/pay cards before Growth. The normal income step follows Growth and uses the highest number then uncovered, including a higher number just revealed by that Growth, so the benefit applies in this same Spirit Phase. Players may plan their choices earlier; planning is not the formal play/pay step.

source_refs.label: CORE p8 Spirit Phase: each Spirit does three things in the following order; Growth then highest-uncovered normal income then play/pay
Primary FAQ Core HTML .7w4g7z1: each individual Spirit must Grow / Gain Energy / Play Power Cards in that order

faq_rulings.rule: It may reposition an existing island Presence instead of taking a track disk even while track disks remain. Empty tracks are not a prerequisite. Choose a normally legal destination using existing Presence, then take an own island disk; this does not uncover a new track benefit.
The normal Power adds Defend 1, not 2: its printed Fear counts but ordinary Town-destruction Fear does not. The 2 Fear from To Dream a Thousand Deaths does count and adds Defend 2.

source_refs.label: effect text and parenthetical Fear-source exception

faq_rulings.rule: Yes. The Spirit using Tidal Boon (Ocean) may move that Dahan to any Coastal land instead of Drowning it; the destination need not be adjacent. This is optional. If the option is not taken, the ordinary Ocean Drowning applies. It applies to this Power’s Push, not later unrelated Pushes.

Wrap’s explicit First instruction Gathers before the base Move, allowing those gathered Dahan to be moved by the base effect and Defend 5 in the destination if at least one moves. Dissolve’s explicit Before Pushing instruction resolves its threshold Damage before the Explorer Push (after the preceding replacements). Such timing words override the default top-to-bottom position; they do not create another Power use.
